note: agent-lifted from VA's manuals (pilot steps 2 and 3)

concepts.label: Transmit laser failure
concepts.gloss: A hardware fault in a transmitting optical laser that stops or invalidates its emitted channel and causes downstream loss of signal.
concepts.example: The laser in a VA-TPD-400 fails, turns off its optical channel, and the far-end receiver reports loss of signal.

concepts.label: Card failure
concepts.gloss: A whole-card hardware failure that removes local receive traffic or transmitted signal and can suppress monitoring and subordinate traffic alarms.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-400 card loses power, its received traffic disappears locally, and the far end loses the channel.

concepts.label: Receiver degradation
concepts.gloss: A deterioration confined to an optical receiver that introduces receive errors while the optical path and other channels remain normal.
concepts.example: One VA-OTN-LC-400 receiver develops excess internal noise and records errors although adjacent channels remain healthy.

concepts.label: Laser ageing
concepts.gloss: Progressive wear of a transmit laser that requires rising laser-bias current and can eventually culminate in transmitter failure.
concepts.example: A transponder's laser bias rises from 100% to 123% of beginning-of-life value before the laser ultimately fails.

concepts.label: Margin erosion
concepts.gloss: A gradual reduction in an optical channel's performance margin, commonly due to cumulative component ageing along its path.
concepts.example: Over several months a receiver's measured channel margin declines slowly from 4 dB to 1.5 dB.

concepts.label: Fibre break
concepts.gloss: A physical cut or discontinuity in an optical fibre that prevents light from traversing the affected span.
concepts.example: Construction work severs an inter-hut fibre, causing receivers beyond the cut to see no light.

concepts.label: EDFA dead
concepts.gloss: A complete EDFA failure in which the amplifier produces no output light and all channels through it are lost.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA loses its pump and emits no optical output, dropping every wavelength on the span.

concepts.label: jumper pulled
concepts.gloss: Disconnection of an optical patch jumper that opens the light path at a patching point.
concepts.example: A technician removes the transponder output jumper, and the remote receiver raises OCH_LOS.

concepts.label: ROADM ingress port blocked
concepts.gloss: A ROADM ingress state or fault that prevents an incoming optical channel from entering the switching fabric.
concepts.example: The ingress WSS blocks a wavelength arriving on degree 2, leaving its destination receiver without light.

concepts.label: high span loss
concepts.gloss: Excessive attenuation across a fibre span that reduces received optical power enough to degrade or lose the carried signal.
concepts.example: A damaged splice adds 8 dB of span loss, leading first to OTU_SD and then OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: Noise figure degradation
concepts.gloss: Deterioration of an EDFA's noise performance that lowers downstream OSNR despite apparently normal amplifier output power.
concepts.example: An ageing pre-amplifier maintains its output level but adds noise, reducing OSNR on every downstream channel.

concepts.label: DGD increase
concepts.gloss: An increase in differential group delay that creates polarization-mode-dispersion impairment on an optical channel.
concepts.example: A fibre route develops 35 ps of DGD, exceeding receiver tolerance and causing OTU frame errors.

concepts.label: WSS passband offset
concepts.gloss: Misalignment of a wavelength-selective switch filter relative to a channel, narrowing or shifting its effective passband and degrading quality without necessarily changing power.
concepts.example: A WSS filter drifts 8 GHz off centre; channel power remains normal but pre-FEC BER rises.

concepts.label: fast SOP event
concepts.gloss: A rapid state-of-polarization transition faster than the coherent receiver can track.
concepts.example: A lightning-induced fibre disturbance rotates SOP abruptly and the receiver temporarily loses OTU framing.

concepts.label: contaminated connector
concepts.gloss: Optical-connector contamination that introduces attenuation or reflection and degrades the associated signal.
concepts.example: Dust on an LC connector raises pre-FEC errors until cleaning restores the channel.

concepts.label: Any failure
concepts.gloss: A generic placeholder for any upstream, path, equipment, or service failure capable of producing the referenced alarm.
concepts.example: OTU_BDI is correlated to any defect reported by the far end when the precise remote fault is unknown.

concepts.label: Gain loss
concepts.gloss: An EDFA fault in which delivered amplification falls below target, causing low output power and degraded downstream OSNR across all channels.
concepts.example: A pre-amplifier provides 12 dB instead of its 18 dB target, lowering all channel powers and OSNR.

concepts.label: Pump ageing
concepts.gloss: Progressive EDFA pump-laser wear that requires increasing drive current to maintain gain and eventually triggers an end-of-life alarm.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-BST pump current climbs to 125% of its beginning-of-life value and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: Gain tilt
concepts.gloss: A wavelength-dependent EDFA gain imbalance that leaves channels near one band edge lower than channels elsewhere in the band.
concepts.example: An amplifier tilt makes the long-wavelength edge channels 3 dB lower than central channels.

concepts.label: previous EDFA dead
concepts.gloss: Failure of the immediately upstream EDFA, identified as the location responsible for missing light at the next amplifier.
concepts.example: AMP_INPUT_LOS on an OLA is traced to the preceding OLA having no output.

concepts.label: OMS input jumper pulled
concepts.gloss: Disconnection of the jumper feeding an optical multiplex section input, removing composite light at that OMS boundary.
concepts.example: The pre-amplifier input jumper is removed during maintenance and OMS_LOS_P is raised.

concepts.label: Fabric failure
concepts.gloss: An internal OTN switch-fabric failure that interrupts all ODUs traversing the switch and forwards ODU-AIS on their cross-connections.
concepts.example: A VA-OTNSW fabric module fails, interrupting every traversing ODU and propagating AIS.

concepts.label: Misconnection
concepts.gloss: An erroneous OTN cross-connect that routes an ODU to the wrong destination without requiring an optical-layer defect.
concepts.example: ODU 7 is provisioned to the wrong client port, where ODU_TIM reports an unexpected trail trace.

concepts.label: Port failure
concepts.gloss: A client-interface port or client-optic hardware failure that takes the attached client service down.
concepts.example: The optic in a VA-CP-100GE port fails and its 100GE client service goes down.

concepts.label: WSS attenuation drift
concepts.gloss: A gradual increase in attenuation applied by a WSS to one channel, causing low power after the node.
concepts.example: A channel's WSS setting creeps from 2 dB to 5 dB and its downstream power falls by 3 dB.

concepts.label: WSS ingress port failure
concepts.gloss: Failure of one WSS ingress port that blocks every channel arriving on its ROADM degree while leaving other degrees unaffected.
concepts.example: Degree 3's WSS input fails, blocking all degree-3 wavelengths at the node while degree 4 continues normally.

concepts.label: No light
concepts.gloss: An optical condition in which no detectable light is present at the observed interface.
concepts.example: The receive photodiode reads below its detection floor after the fibre is unplugged.

concepts.label: dLOS
concepts.gloss: A digital loss-of-signal condition indicating that the receiver cannot detect a valid digital signal stream.
concepts.example: A line card asserts dLOS when incoming symbols disappear even though its interface remains enabled.

concepts.label: Loss of OTU frame
concepts.gloss: A condition in which an OTN receiver cannot acquire or maintain valid OTU frame alignment.
concepts.example: Severe channel noise prevents the receiver from locating OTU frame boundaries and it declares loss of frame.

concepts.label: Card failure
concepts.gloss: The observed state that a hardware card is nonfunctional rather than merely carrying a degraded channel.
concepts.example: A shelf reports the line card absent and failed after its processor stops responding.

concepts.label: dEQ
concepts.gloss: A degrade-quality indication that the received digital signal has crossed the equipment's configured quality-degradation criterion.
concepts.example: The receiver asserts dEQ after pre-FEC errors remain above the degradation threshold.

concepts.label: traffic alarms masked by the equipment alarm
concepts.gloss: A state in which a dominant equipment alarm suppresses or hides subordinate traffic alarms that would otherwise be reported.
concepts.example: EQPT_CARD_FAIL remains visible while individual LOS and frame alarms on that failed card are masked.

concepts.label: Degraded light: low power, low OSNR, high DGD, passband penalty, receiver penalty, slow margin decline
concepts.gloss: Received light that remains present but has impaired power, OSNR, DGD, filter passband, receiver performance, or channel margin.
concepts.example: A channel still carries light but has low OSNR and declining margin, producing increasing pre-FEC errors.

concepts.label: Pre-FEC errors once the degradation is larger than the channel margin
concepts.gloss: Pre-FEC errors appearing after aggregate optical degradation exceeds the channel's available operating margin.
concepts.example: A 2.5 dB penalty exceeds a channel's 2 dB margin and measurable pre-FEC BER begins.

concepts.label: loss of frame if much larger
concepts.gloss: Loss of frame arising when an already degraded signal impairment becomes substantially larger than the receiver's tolerance.
concepts.example: Further OSNR decline changes a degraded-but-framed OTU into OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: Fast SOP change beyond tracking speed
concepts.gloss: A polarization change whose rate exceeds the coherent receiver's tracking capability.
concepts.example: SOP rotates faster than the DSP can follow, causing a burst of frame errors.

concepts.label: Errored seconds
concepts.gloss: Seconds during which one or more monitored transmission errors occur on the signal.
concepts.example: A receiver records 12 errored seconds in a 15-minute interval after intermittent noise bursts.

concepts.label: ODU-AIS is sent downstream
concepts.gloss: The consequent OTN state in which ODU alarm-indication signal is transmitted downstream after an upstream OTU defect.
concepts.example: Following OTU_LOF, the line card inserts ODU-AIS into every contained ODU.

concepts.label: OTU-BDI is returned
concepts.gloss: The consequent OTN state in which backward defect indication is sent toward the far-end OTU transmitter.
concepts.example: A receiver losing OTU framing returns OTU-BDI to the transmitting line card.

concepts.label: Laser off or failed
concepts.gloss: A channel state in which its transmit laser is deliberately off or has failed to emit usable light.
concepts.example: The channel laser reports enabled but emits no power after a hardware failure.

concepts.label: loss of signal
concepts.gloss: Absence of the transmitted optical channel as observed at the far-end receiver or endpoint.
concepts.example: When the local transmit laser fails, the remote receiver raises loss of signal for that wavelength.

concepts.label: received traffic lost
concepts.gloss: Local disappearance of traffic that should have been received by a card or interface.
concepts.example: A failed receive-side card stops delivering its incoming client traffic locally.

concepts.label: monitoring silent
concepts.gloss: Loss of telemetry or supervision output from equipment that is no longer reporting its monitored state.
concepts.example: After a card processor fails, no performance counters or status updates are emitted.

concepts.label: Errors
concepts.gloss: Transmission errors confined to the affected receiver rather than shared by the optical path or other channels.
concepts.example: One receiver logs symbol errors while another receiver on the same optical channel is normal.

concepts.label: normal
concepts.gloss: An unaffected state in which the referenced optical path or other channels continue to meet expected operation.
concepts.example: A degraded receiver reports errors, but the optical path and neighbouring wavelengths remain normal.

concepts.label: LBC rising
concepts.gloss: An increasing laser-bias-current measurement indicating that the transmitter is driving its laser harder to maintain output.
concepts.example: LBC rises steadily from 100% to 118% as the transmit laser ages.

concepts.label: precedes transmit laser failure
concepts.gloss: A predictive state that occurs before likely transmit-laser failure rather than representing the final failure itself.
concepts.example: Sustained high laser bias provides warning weeks before the transmitter stops emitting.

concepts.label: Slow decline of the channel's margin, usually from ageing of components along the path
concepts.gloss: A gradual reduction of receiver-observed channel margin over time, typically reflecting ageing along the path.
concepts.example: Daily measurements show channel margin falling by 0.1 dB per month at the receiver.

concepts.label: No light at the receiver
concepts.gloss: No detectable optical carrier at a channel receiver input.
concepts.example: A receiver reads no input power and raises OCH_LOS after an upstream jumper is removed.

concepts.label: OTU frame lost, light present
concepts.gloss: Loss of OTU frame alignment while optical light is still detected, distinguishing quality failure from optical absence.
concepts.example: The receiver measures -8 dBm but cannot frame the noisy OTU and raises OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: Errors above the degrade threshold (margin under about 1 dB)
concepts.gloss: A received-error level above the signal-degrade threshold, typically corresponding to less than about 1 dB channel margin.
concepts.example: Pre-FEC BER crosses the configured limit when estimated margin falls to 0.7 dB.

concepts.label: Far end reports a defect on this card's transmitted signal
concepts.gloss: An indication returned by the remote endpoint that it detects a defect in this card's transmitted OTU signal.
concepts.example: The local card raises OTU_BDI after the remote receiver reports loss of frame.

concepts.label: Transmit laser fault detected
concepts.gloss: An equipment-detected malfunction of the optical transmit laser.
concepts.example: Internal supervision detects missing laser output and raises EQPT_TX_FAIL.

concepts.label: Card hardware fault
concepts.gloss: An internally detected physical or electronic fault affecting an equipment card.
concepts.example: A failed card power rail triggers EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

concepts.label: LBC above 120 % of beginning of life (internal supervision)
concepts.gloss: A laser-bias-current reading above 120 percent of its beginning-of-life reference, used as an internal ageing threshold.
concepts.example: A transmitter with LBC at 123% raises LASER_BIAS_HIGH.

concepts.label: The EDFA cards run in automatic gain control (AGC).
concepts.gloss: The operating state in which an EDFA automatically adjusts pump drive to hold a configured gain.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA increases pump current to preserve 18 dB gain when its input level changes.

concepts.label: The gain target is provisioned at turn-up equal to the attenuation of the fibre span ahead of the card.
concepts.gloss: The turn-up configuration in which an EDFA's gain target is set equal to the attenuation of the following fibre span.
concepts.example: For a measured 17 dB span loss, the booster is provisioned with a 17 dB gain target.

concepts.label: Under AGC, a drop of input level
concepts.gloss: A reduction in EDFA input level while the amplifier remains in automatic gain-control mode.
concepts.example: A 3 dB upstream power reduction lowers composite input from -10 dBm to -13 dBm.

concepts.label: an equal drop of output level
concepts.gloss: A decrease in EDFA output level equal to an input decrease when constant gain is maintained.
concepts.example: With gain fixed at 18 dB, a 3 dB input drop produces a 3 dB output drop.

concepts.label: the optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR) of all channels degrades with it
concepts.gloss: A simultaneous decline in optical signal-to-noise ratio for all channels affected by an amplifier or line-power change.
concepts.example: After amplifier input falls, OSNR decreases by 2 dB across the entire WDM band.

concepts.label: A card with no input light
concepts.gloss: An amplifier or optical card state in which its input power detector sees no incoming light.
concepts.example: An OLA reports no input after the preceding span is cut.

concepts.label: no output light
concepts.gloss: Absence of composite optical output from an amplifier, affecting every channel it should emit.
concepts.example: A dead EDFA has normal input but zero output, removing all WDM channels.

concepts.label: Other conditions at the input
concepts.gloss: Input-side optical properties or impairments other than total light loss that arrive at a card.
concepts.example: Low OSNR and unequal channel powers enter an otherwise functioning amplifier.

concepts.label: are passed through to the output
concepts.gloss: Propagation of incoming optical conditions through a device to its output rather than their removal by that device.
concepts.example: An input OSNR penalty remains present at the amplifier output.

concepts.label: Every hut terminates the optical supervisory channel (OSC) and launches its own OSC onto the next span
concepts.gloss: The span-local OSC arrangement in which each amplifier hut terminates the incoming supervisory channel and originates a new one for the next span.
concepts.example: Hut B receives Hut A's OSC, terminates it, and launches a fresh OSC toward Hut C.

concepts.label: an OSC failure is confined to the span on which it occurs
concepts.gloss: An OSC failure state whose effect is limited to the single span where the supervisory channel is missing.
concepts.example: Loss of the B-to-C OSC does not prevent Hut C from launching its own OSC toward Hut D.

concepts.label: all channels lost
concepts.gloss: Simultaneous loss of every optical wavelength traversing the affected element or section.
concepts.example: Failure of an in-line EDFA removes all 80 channels from the next span.

concepts.label: low output
concepts.gloss: Composite amplifier output below its expected or provisioned level across all carried channels.
concepts.example: An EDFA gain fault lowers every output wavelength by 4 dB.

concepts.label: OSNR down
concepts.gloss: Reduced optical signal-to-noise ratio affecting all relevant channels and persisting at downstream observation points.
concepts.example: A noisy EDFA lowers OSNR on every channel measured at the next ROADM.

concepts.label: output power normal
concepts.gloss: An amplifier state in which output power remains at its expected level even though another quality metric may be degraded.
concepts.example: The EDFA output is still +20 dBm while its degraded noise figure lowers OSNR.

concepts.label: PUMP-I climbs to maintain gain
concepts.gloss: A rise in an EDFA card's pump-laser drive current as its control loop compensates to maintain gain.
concepts.example: PUMP-I on one VA-OA-PRE rises from 100% to 116% while output gain remains stable.

concepts.label: ends in the end-of-life alarm
concepts.gloss: The terminal ageing state in which rising pump demand causes an end-of-life alarm on the affected EDFA card.
concepts.example: When PUMP-I reaches 121%, the same card raises AMP_PUMP_EOL.

concepts.label: channels low
concepts.gloss: Reduced optical power on channels clustered at one edge of the wavelength band, characteristic of gain tilt.
concepts.example: The five longest-wavelength channels measure 3 dB below the centre channels.

concepts.label: Loss of light at IN-PWR
concepts.gloss: Loss of optical light reported by an amplifier's input-power monitoring point.
concepts.example: The OLA IN-PWR detector drops below threshold and raises AMP_INPUT_LOS.

concepts.label: OSC not received
concepts.gloss: Failure of a site to receive the optical supervisory channel from the preceding span.
concepts.example: A pre-amplifier detects no incoming OSC after a span fibre cut.

concepts.label: No light at OUT-PWR with input light present
concepts.gloss: No optical output at an amplifier's OUT-PWR monitor despite detectable input light.
concepts.example: An EDFA receives -12 dBm input but reports no output and raises AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: Gain more than 2 dB from target
concepts.gloss: Measured amplifier gain differing from its configured target by more than 2 dB.
concepts.example: An EDFA targeted at 18 dB delivers 15.5 dB and raises AMP_GAIN_OOR.

concepts.label: PUMP-I above 120 % of beginning of life
concepts.gloss: An EDFA pump-current measurement exceeding 120 percent of its beginning-of-life reference.
concepts.example: PUMP-I reaches 124% on a pre-amplifier and triggers its end-of-life alarm.

concepts.label: The switch forwards ODU-AIS on each ODU it cross-connects.
concepts.gloss: The OTN switch behavior of forwarding ODU-AIS on every ODU that it cross-connects.
concepts.example: An AIS-bearing ODU entering VA-OTNSW leaves on its provisioned egress still carrying AIS.

concepts.label: ODU-AIS
concepts.gloss: Presence of the ODU-layer alarm indication signal used to notify downstream equipment of an upstream defect.
concepts.example: A client port receives ODU-AIS after the upstream OTU loses framing.

concepts.label: a misdirected ODU
concepts.gloss: An ODU delivered along an incorrect cross-connect path or to an unintended endpoint.
concepts.example: The ODU for client A arrives at client B's port and produces a trace-identifier mismatch.

concepts.label: the client service down
concepts.gloss: Loss of usable connectivity for the client service carried by the affected port or ODU.
concepts.example: The customer's 100GE service stops passing frames after its client optic fails.

concepts.label: ODU-AIS or a misdirected ODU
concepts.gloss: A received ODU state in which the payload is either replaced by AIS or belongs to the wrong connection.
concepts.example: The client port sees ODU-AIS after a fabric defect, or an unexpected trail trace after misconnection.

concepts.label: SNCP is configured
concepts.gloss: A protection configuration in which a client service has paired working and protection ODU paths selected at reception.
concepts.example: A 100GE service is provisioned over two diverse ODUs with SNCP selection at the destination port.

concepts.label: the selector has a defect-free path to choose
concepts.gloss: Availability of at least one SNCP member path without a detected defect for the receiver selector to use.
concepts.example: When the working ODU fails, the selector chooses the healthy protection ODU.

concepts.label: the service takes a hit only
concepts.gloss: A brief service interruption incurred during protection switching rather than a sustained outage.
concepts.example: The client loses traffic for 30 ms while SNCP changes to the protection path.

concepts.label: interrupted
concepts.gloss: Loss of traffic continuity for all ODUs traversing an OTN switch.
concepts.example: A switch-fabric reset interrupts every ODU cross-connected through VA-OTNSW.

concepts.label: ODU-AIS forwarded
concepts.gloss: Propagation of ODU-AIS on each affected cross-connected ODU beyond the switch.
concepts.example: The failed fabric causes AIS to be emitted on each ODU egress.

concepts.label: cross-connected to the wrong destination
concepts.gloss: A single ODU being cross-connected to an endpoint other than its provisioned destination.
concepts.example: ODU-12 intended for port 4 is mistakenly connected to port 7.

concepts.label: no optical symptom
concepts.gloss: Absence of an optical-layer power or quality indication for a logical ODU routing defect.
concepts.example: A misdirected ODU has normal light and OSNR, so only OTN trace monitoring reveals the fault.

concepts.label: failed
concepts.gloss: A nonoperational state of the client optic or physical client port.
concepts.example: A VA-CP-400GE reports its pluggable optic failed and cannot transmit.

concepts.label: down
concepts.gloss: An unavailable state of the client service associated with a failed port or optic.
concepts.example: The 400GE service is operationally down after its client port fails.

concepts.label: Switching is per channel
concepts.gloss: ROADM operation in which each wavelength is independently selected and routed at an egress degree.
concepts.example: At one ROADM, channel 21 is sent east while channel 22 is sent south.

concepts.label: A line-wide impairment on an ingress degree therefore continues as a per-channel impairment on each channel routed onward.
concepts.gloss: A common ingress-line impairment that becomes attached to each individually switched channel routed onward from that ingress degree.
concepts.example: Low OSNR on the west ingress remains on each west-originating wavelength sent to different egress degrees.

concepts.label: An upstream power loss within that range
concepts.gloss: An upstream optical power reduction that remains within the downstream node's leveling or compensation range.
concepts.example: A 2 dB input loss lies within the ROADM's 4 dB leveling capability.

concepts.label: is levelled out at the node
concepts.gloss: A power variation that the node compensates so the affected channel leaves at its configured output level.
concepts.example: The ROADM adds 2 dB less attenuation and restores a weakened channel to its target power.

concepts.label: the OSNR penalty it caused stays
concepts.gloss: Persistence of an upstream OSNR degradation even after a node restores the channel's optical power.
concepts.example: The ROADM levels power to -2 dBm, but the channel retains its 2 dB OSNR penalty.

concepts.label: a larger loss
concepts.gloss: An upstream power reduction exceeding the node's available leveling or compensation range.
concepts.example: A 7 dB loss exceeds the WSS's 4 dB correction range.

concepts.label: is passed on as low power
concepts.gloss: Propagation of an uncompensated input loss as low channel power beyond the node.
concepts.example: After compensation is exhausted, the channel exits the ROADM 3 dB below target.

concepts.label: passes through
concepts.gloss: An impairment state that continues through an optical node rather than being terminated there.
concepts.example: A channel's OSNR degradation remains after it traverses the ROADM.

concepts.label: Attenuation creeps above its setting
concepts.gloss: Gradual drift of a WSS channel's applied attenuation above its configured setting.
concepts.example: The WSS attenuation for channel 37 slowly rises from 3.0 dB to 4.2 dB.

concepts.label: low in power
concepts.gloss: Below-target power on the affected channel as measured after the node.
concepts.example: Channel 37 is measured at -6 dBm after the ROADM instead of its -3 dBm target.

concepts.label: Passband shifted
concepts.gloss: Displacement of one channel's WSS filter passband away from the channel's nominal centre frequency.
concepts.example: The filter centre shifts from 193.1 THz to 193.108 THz for one wavelength.

concepts.label: Passband narrowed
concepts.gloss: Reduction in the usable WSS filter bandwidth presented to one optical channel.
concepts.example: A nominal 50 GHz passband narrows enough to clip a 400G signal's spectrum.

concepts.label: power normal
concepts.gloss: Expected measured optical power on one channel despite a possible spectral-filter or signal-quality defect.
concepts.example: The impaired channel still reads -2 dBm even though its shifted passband increases errors.

concepts.label: signal quality down
concepts.gloss: Degraded recoverability or error performance of one channel despite continued signal presence.
concepts.example: A channel retains normal power but its pre-FEC BER rises after passband clipping.

concepts.label: fails
concepts.gloss: Loss of functional operation of one WSS input port.
concepts.example: The degree-2 WSS input ceases passing or switching any incoming wavelengths.

concepts.label: blocked
concepts.gloss: Prevention at a ROADM node of all channels arriving through the affected ingress degree from passing onward.
concepts.example: All wavelengths from the north degree disappear at the node after its ingress port fails.

concepts.label: unaffected
concepts.gloss: Continued normal operation of ROADM degrees other than the degree containing the failed WSS input.
concepts.example: The east-degree channels continue through normally while the north ingress is blocked.

concepts.label: Received optical power
concepts.gloss: The optical power level measured at a receiver input, available as standard telemetry or under power monitoring.
concepts.example: A VA-TPD-400 reports received power of -9.4 dBm.

concepts.label: errored seconds
concepts.gloss: A performance counter of one-second intervals containing at least one monitored transmission error.
concepts.example: The line card reports 6 errored seconds during the last 15 minutes.

concepts.label: OSNR
concepts.gloss: The measured ratio of optical signal power to optical noise power for a channel, available with advanced monitoring or an OCM.
concepts.example: The ROADM OCM measures channel OSNR at 18.7 dB.

concepts.label: pre-FEC BER
concepts.gloss: The bit-error rate measured before forward-error correction by a coherent receiver.
concepts.example: A muxponder reports a pre-FEC BER of 2×10^-4.

concepts.label: DGD
concepts.gloss: Measured differential group delay between polarization modes of the received optical signal.
concepts.example: Advanced monitoring reports DGD of 22 ps on the 400G channel.

concepts.label: SOP rate of change
concepts.gloss: The measured rate at which the received optical state of polarization changes.
concepts.example: The receiver records an SOP change rate above its tracking threshold during a fibre disturbance.

concepts.label: Transmit laser bias current, % of beginning of life
concepts.gloss: Transmit-laser bias current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life reference value.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-200 reports laser bias at 117% of beginning-of-life current.

concepts.label: Composite input power
concepts.gloss: Total optical power of all WDM channels entering an amplifier card.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA reports composite input power of -8 dBm.

concepts.label: Composite output power
concepts.gloss: Total optical power of all WDM channels leaving an amplifier card.
concepts.example: The booster reports composite output power of +20 dBm.

concepts.label: Pump laser drive current, % of beginning of life
concepts.gloss: EDFA pump-laser drive current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
concepts.example: A pre-amplifier reports pump drive current at 121%.

concepts.label: OSC receiver status
concepts.gloss: The receive status of the optical supervisory channel at an amplifier site.
concepts.example: The OLA reports OSC receiver status as not received after a span cut.

concepts.label: client ES
concepts.gloss: The client-interface errored-seconds counter retained in standard 15-minute performance bins.
concepts.example: A VA-CP-100GE records 14 client ES in the current bin.

concepts.label: client UAS
concepts.gloss: The client-interface unavailable-seconds counter retained in standard 15-minute performance bins.
concepts.example: A failed client port accumulates 300 UAS in a 15-minute interval.

concepts.label: Per-channel power
concepts.gloss: Optical power measured separately for each wavelength by an optical channel monitor.
concepts.example: The ROADM OCM reports channel 44 at -3.1 dBm.

concepts.label: VA-TPD-400
concepts.gloss: The VA 400G transponder resource that terminates a coherent channel, exposes optical performance measurements, and can experience transmitter, receiver, laser-ageing, or card faults.
concepts.example: A VA-TPD-400 carries one 400G wavelength and reports received power, OSNR, pre-FEC BER, DGD, SOP rate, and laser bias.

concepts.label: VA-MXP-200
concepts.gloss: The VA 200G muxponder resource that aggregates client traffic onto a coherent line channel and provides line-quality and laser-health telemetry.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-200 maps clients into a 200G wavelength and raises OCH_LOS when that wavelength disappears.

concepts.label: VA-MXP-400
concepts.gloss: The VA 400G muxponder resource that aggregates client traffic onto a 400G coherent channel while monitoring its optical and error performance.
concepts.example: A VA-MXP-400 reports rising pre-FEC BER and OSNR decline on its 400G line signal.

concepts.label: VA-OTN-LC-200
concepts.gloss: The VA 200G OTN line card that terminates an OTU/optical channel and monitors receiver quality and transmit-laser health.
concepts.example: A VA-OTN-LC-200 receives an OTU, measures DGD and BER, and raises OTU_LOF when framing is lost.

concepts.label: VA-OTN-LC-400
concepts.gloss: The VA 400G OTN line card that terminates a 400G OTU channel and provides coherent optical, error, and laser-health measurements.
concepts.example: A VA-OTN-LC-400 reports -8 dBm received power and raises LASER_BIAS_HIGH at 122% bias.

concepts.label: EDFA card
concepts.gloss: The family of VA erbium-doped fibre-amplifier cards used as boosters, in-line amplifiers, or pre-amplifiers and monitored for power, pump, gain, noise, and OSC faults.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA measures composite input and output power and raises AMP_PUMP_EOL when its pump ages.

concepts.label: transmit-side EDFA (booster), fitted at the head end of each optical multiplex section (OMS)
concepts.gloss: A transmit-side EDFA located at the head of an optical multiplex section to launch amplified WDM power into the span.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-BST amplifies ROADM output before the first fibre span.

concepts.label: optical line amplifier (OLA), fitted at in-line amplifier huts
concepts.gloss: An in-line optical line amplifier installed at an intermediate hut to restore optical power between terminal sites.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA at Hut 3 amplifies all channels before the next span.

concepts.label: receive-side EDFA (pre-amp), fitted at the tail end of each OMS
concepts.gloss: A receive-side EDFA at the tail of an optical multiplex section that amplifies incoming WDM light before reception or switching.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-PRE amplifies the incoming span immediately before the terminal ROADM.

concepts.label: OTN cross-connect switch
concepts.gloss: A VA OTN cross-connect that switches ODUs between ports and can suffer fabric-wide interruption or individual ODU misconnection.
concepts.example: VA-OTNSW cross-connects ODU-4 to a client port and raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL if its fabric fails.

concepts.label: client interface port
concepts.gloss: A VA Ethernet-facing client interface that terminates a client optic, measures client performance, and can report port or carried-service failure.
concepts.example: A VA-CP-100GE connects a customer router and records client ES and UAS.

concepts.label: colourless, directionless, contentionless ROADM
concepts.gloss: A colourless, directionless, contentionless VA ROADM that independently routes wavelengths and monitors per-channel power and OSNR.
concepts.example: VA-ROADM-CDC switches a wavelength from the west ingress to the south egress while its OCM measures power.

concepts.label: one WSS module per degree
concepts.gloss: The wavelength-selective-switch module serving one directional degree of a ROADM.
concepts.example: The WSS module for the north degree filters and routes all wavelengths arriving from the north span.

concepts.label: OCH_LOS
concepts.gloss: A channel loss-of-signal alarm raised by a coherent receiver when no light is detected, with possible upstream laser, card, fibre, amplifier, jumper, or ROADM causes.
concepts.example: A VA-TPD-400 raises OCH_LOS after a fibre cut removes light at its receiver.

concepts.label: OTU_LOF
concepts.gloss: An OTU loss-of-frame alarm raised when light remains present but signal quality is too poor to maintain OTU framing.
concepts.example: A channel with severe OSNR degradation still measures optical power but raises OTU_LOF.

concepts.label: OTU_SD
concepts.gloss: An OTU signal-degrade alarm raised when received errors exceed the configured degradation threshold before framing is fully lost.
concepts.example: A dirty connector reduces margin below 1 dB and the receiver raises OTU_SD.

concepts.label: OTU_BDI
concepts.gloss: An OTU backward-defect-indication alarm showing that the far-end receiver has detected a defect in the local transmitter's signal.
concepts.example: The local line card raises OTU_BDI when the remote endpoint loses OTU framing.

concepts.label: EQPT_TX_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An equipment alarm reporting an internally detected transmit-laser failure.
concepts.example: A failed laser in a VA-MXP-400 causes EQPT_TX_FAIL on that card.

concepts.label: EQPT_CARD_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An equipment alarm reporting a hardware failure of the entire card.
concepts.example: A line-card power-rail fault raises EQPT_CARD_FAIL and masks its traffic alarms.

concepts.label: LASER_BIAS_HIGH
concepts.gloss: A predictive transmitter alarm raised when laser-bias current exceeds 120 percent of its beginning-of-life value.
concepts.example: LASER_BIAS_HIGH is raised when a transponder reports LBC of 124%.

concepts.label: AMP_INPUT_LOS
concepts.gloss: An OLA input-loss alarm indicating that its IN-PWR monitor detects no incoming span light.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-ILA raises AMP_INPUT_LOS after the preceding EDFA dies.

concepts.label: OMS_LOS_P
concepts.gloss: A pre-amplifier alarm indicating loss of composite OMS light at its input.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-PRE raises OMS_LOS_P when the OMS input jumper is pulled.

concepts.label: OSC_LOS
concepts.gloss: An amplifier-site alarm indicating that the incoming optical supervisory channel is not being received on the span.
concepts.example: An OLA raises OSC_LOS after excessive span loss removes the OSC.

concepts.label: AMP_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An EDFA failure alarm raised when input light is present but no optical output is produced.
concepts.example: A booster with normal input and a dead pump raises AMP_FAIL.

concepts.label: AMP_GAIN_OOR
concepts.gloss: An amplifier alarm raised when measured gain differs from target by more than 2 dB.
concepts.example: AMP_GAIN_OOR is raised when a target of 20 dB yields only 17 dB.

concepts.label: AMP_PUMP_EOL
concepts.gloss: An EDFA pump end-of-life alarm raised when pump current exceeds 120 percent of its beginning-of-life value.
concepts.example: A VA-OA-PRE raises AMP_PUMP_EOL at 123% pump current.

concepts.label: CLIENT_SF
concepts.gloss: A client signal-fail alarm raised at a client port when a port, ODU path, switch fabric, misconnection, or other failure prevents valid client service.
concepts.example: A VA-CP-100GE raises CLIENT_SF when its ODU is replaced by AIS.

concepts.label: ODU_AIS
concepts.gloss: An alarm at a client port indicating receipt of ODU alarm-indication signal from an upstream defect.
concepts.example: The destination client port raises ODU_AIS after the source OTU loses frame.

concepts.label: ODU_BDI
concepts.gloss: An ODU-layer backward-defect-indication alarm reported at a client port for a defect signaled from the remote ODU endpoint.
concepts.example: A client port raises ODU_BDI after the far-end ODU sink detects a service defect.

concepts.label: ODU_TIM
concepts.gloss: An ODU trail-trace-identifier mismatch alarm, commonly indicating that the ODU has been misconnected.
concepts.example: ODU_TIM is raised when a port receives another service's expected trace value.

concepts.label: PROT_ACTIVE
concepts.gloss: A protection-state alarm indicating that the client service is currently selected from its protection ODU path rather than the working path.
concepts.example: After the working ODU fails, the client port switches paths and raises PROT_ACTIVE.

concepts.label: PROT_UNAVAIL
concepts.gloss: A protection-state alarm indicating that no usable protection path is available for the client service.
concepts.example: PROT_UNAVAIL is raised when both SNCP paths are defective.

concepts.label: EQPT_PORT_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An equipment alarm indicating hardware failure of the client port or its optic.
concepts.example: A failed VA-CP-400GE optic causes EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

concepts.label: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL
concepts.gloss: An OTN-switch alarm indicating failure of the cross-connect fabric and potential interruption of all traversing ODUs.
concepts.example: VA-OTNSW raises OTN_FABRIC_FAIL when its switching matrix stops forwarding ODUs.

concepts.label: the channel
concepts.gloss: The single optical wavelength channel directly affected by a condition.
concepts.example: A failed transmit laser removes only its associated 193.1 THz channel.

concepts.label: the transmitted channel
concepts.gloss: The particular outbound optical channel emitted by the referenced transmitter.
concepts.example: Card failure causes loss of the card's transmitted 400G wavelength at the far end.

concepts.label: received traffic
concepts.gloss: Traffic arriving at and expected to be delivered by the referenced receiving equipment.
concepts.example: A card failure discards all received traffic destined for its local client interfaces.

concepts.label: monitoring
concepts.gloss: The telemetry, supervision, and status-reporting functions of the referenced equipment.
concepts.example: A dead card processor makes its power and performance monitoring silent.

concepts.label: traffic alarms
concepts.gloss: Service- and signal-layer alarms subordinate to a dominant equipment fault.
concepts.example: LOS and OTU_LOF are masked while EQPT_CARD_FAIL is active.

concepts.label: this receiver only
concepts.gloss: Only the particular receiver observing the condition, excluding the shared path and other receivers.
concepts.example: Internal receiver noise produces errors on receiver A but not receiver B.

concepts.label: other channels
concepts.gloss: Optical channels other than the specifically impaired channel or receiver.
concepts.example: Neighbouring wavelengths remain normal during a single-channel receiver fault.

concepts.label: the optical path
concepts.gloss: The end-to-end optical route carrying the referenced channel through fibres, amplifiers, and ROADMs.
concepts.example: Path power and OSNR remain normal despite a fault internal to one receiver.

concepts.label: LBC
concepts.gloss: The transmit laser-bias-current indicator used to assess laser ageing.
concepts.example: The affected scope is the card's LBC value rising from 100% to 120%.

concepts.label: transmit laser failure
concepts.gloss: The future or actual transmit-laser failure event for which an ageing condition provides warning.
concepts.example: High LBC is treated as a precursor scoped to eventual transmit-laser failure.

concepts.label: the channel's margin
concepts.gloss: The performance headroom of one optical channel before error or framing thresholds are crossed.
concepts.example: The channel's margin declines from 3 dB to 0.8 dB.

concepts.label: all channels
concepts.gloss: Every wavelength traversing the affected common optical element or section.
concepts.example: An EDFA outage removes all 80 channels rather than one wavelength.

concepts.label: every channel downstream
concepts.gloss: All channels observed beyond the faulty element in the direction of signal propagation.
concepts.example: A degraded amplifier lowers OSNR for every wavelength at downstream ROADMs.

concepts.label: this card
concepts.gloss: The specific equipment card whose local state or telemetry is being described.
concepts.example: Pump current rises on one VA-OA-PRE while other amplifier cards remain normal.

concepts.label: channels at one band edge
concepts.gloss: The subset of WDM channels located near one edge of the amplifier's supported spectral band.
concepts.example: Gain tilt lowers only the longest-wavelength edge channels.

concepts.label: All ODUs
concepts.gloss: Every optical data unit cross-connected through the affected OTN switch.
concepts.example: A fabric failure interrupts all ODUs traversing VA-OTNSW.

concepts.label: each
concepts.gloss: Every individual member of the contextually referenced set, considered separately.
concepts.example: The switch forwards AIS on each cross-connected ODU.

concepts.label: One ODU
concepts.gloss: A single ODU connection rather than all ODUs or the underlying optical channel.
concepts.example: A bad cross-connect misdirects one ODU while others remain correct.

concepts.label: Client optic
concepts.gloss: The optical transceiver component installed on a client-facing interface.
concepts.example: The QSFP optic in a VA-CP-100GE is the failed component.

concepts.label: port
concepts.gloss: The complete physical or logical client interface on the equipment.
concepts.example: EQPT_PORT_FAIL applies to port 3 of the client card.

concepts.label: client service
concepts.gloss: The customer-facing service carried through the referenced client port and ODU connection.
concepts.example: A port failure takes the attached 100GE client service down.

concepts.label: one channel
concepts.gloss: Exactly one wavelength selected by a per-channel WSS function.
concepts.example: A drifting WSS attenuation setting lowers only channel 37.

concepts.label: that channel
concepts.gloss: The same previously identified optical channel affected by the associated fault.
concepts.example: After channel 37's attenuation drifts, that channel is low in power downstream.

concepts.label: One WSS input port
concepts.gloss: One physical or logical ingress port of a wavelength-selective switch.
concepts.example: The north-degree WSS input port fails while its other inputs remain operational.

concepts.label: all channels arriving on that degree
concepts.gloss: All optical channels entering a ROADM on one directional degree.
concepts.example: Failure of the west ingress blocks every wavelength arriving from the west span.

concepts.label: other degrees
concepts.gloss: ROADM directional degrees other than the degree containing the referenced failure.
concepts.example: North and south degrees remain unaffected by failure of the west ingress.

concepts.label: the far-end receiver
concepts.gloss: The remote optical receiver at the opposite end of the transmitted channel.
concepts.example: Loss of signal appears at the far-end receiver after the local laser fails.

concepts.label: Far-end
concepts.gloss: The remote endpoint opposite the equipment or interface under discussion.
concepts.example: The far end raises LOS when no channel reaches it.

concepts.label: locally
concepts.gloss: At the same node or card where the originating observation is made.
concepts.example: Received traffic is lost locally when the card's receive circuitry fails.

concepts.label: the receiver
concepts.gloss: The optical receive endpoint where channel power, margin, and quality are evaluated.
concepts.example: Slow margin decline is observed by telemetry at the receiver.

concepts.label: Far-end transmitter
concepts.gloss: The remote transmitter that sends the signal toward the local receiver.
concepts.example: OTU-BDI is returned to the far-end transmitter after local loss of frame.

concepts.label: Anywhere upstream on the channel's path
concepts.gloss: Any point before the observing receiver along the channel's direction of propagation.
concepts.example: OCH_LOS may originate from a fibre cut anywhere upstream of the receiver.

concepts.label: Upstream on the path
concepts.gloss: The portion of the optical route preceding the current observation point.
concepts.example: A dirty connector on the upstream path reduces received OSNR.

concepts.label: This card
concepts.gloss: The particular equipment card serving as the reference point for an observation or fault.
concepts.example: Internal supervision reports the laser fault on this card.

concepts.label: on the path to the far end
concepts.gloss: A point along the route leading from the current node toward the remote endpoint.
concepts.example: A failed amplifier on the path to the far end removes the transmitted channel.

concepts.label: downstream
concepts.gloss: At nodes or receivers after the referenced element in the signal-flow direction.
concepts.example: OSNR degradation from an EDFA is visible downstream at the next ROADM.

concepts.label: this card
concepts.gloss: The same card on which the condition is generated, measured, or alarmed.
concepts.example: Rising PUMP-I and AMP_PUMP_EOL both appear on this amplifier card.

concepts.label: one band edge
concepts.gloss: One spectral edge of the WDM band supported by an amplifier or line system.
concepts.example: Low-power channels cluster at the long-wavelength band edge.

concepts.label: on the incoming span
concepts.gloss: On the fibre span delivering optical signals into the current site.
concepts.example: A cut on the incoming span causes the OLA input to lose light.

concepts.label: previous EDFA
concepts.gloss: The immediately preceding amplifier in the direction of optical propagation.
concepts.example: The current OLA's input loss is traced to the previous EDFA being dead.

concepts.label: OMS input
concepts.gloss: The ingress boundary where composite WDM light enters an optical multiplex section endpoint.
concepts.example: A pulled jumper at the OMS input causes the pre-amplifier to raise OMS_LOS_P.

concepts.label: the incoming span
concepts.gloss: The fibre section terminating at the current amplifier, ROADM, or receiver site.
concepts.example: OSC_LOS indicates a supervisory-channel problem on the incoming span.

concepts.label: through the switch
concepts.gloss: Along ODU connections that traverse the OTN cross-connect fabric.
concepts.example: All ODUs through the switch are interrupted by a fabric failure.

concepts.label: on the active ODU path
concepts.gloss: The ODU path currently selected to carry the protected client service.
concepts.example: A defect on the active ODU path causes the SNCP selector to change inputs.

concepts.label: at either end
concepts.gloss: At either endpoint of an end-to-end ODU or client-service connection.
concepts.example: A client failure at either end can take the service down.

concepts.label: at a switch on the ODU path
concepts.gloss: At an OTN switching node located on the ODU's routed path.
concepts.example: A misconnection at a switch on the ODU path sends the service to the wrong port.

concepts.label: on the working ODU path
concepts.gloss: On the primary ODU route of an SNCP-protected service.
concepts.example: A fibre defect occurs on the working ODU path and triggers selection of protection.

concepts.label: on the protection ODU path
concepts.gloss: On the alternate ODU route reserved to protect an SNCP service.
concepts.example: PROT_UNAVAIL is raised when the protection ODU path is also defective.

concepts.label: This port
concepts.gloss: The particular client interface port serving as the reference for a fault or alarm.
concepts.example: EQPT_PORT_FAIL identifies the hardware fault on this port.

concepts.label: This switch
concepts.gloss: The particular OTN cross-connect serving as the reference for a fabric or routing fault.
concepts.example: OTN_FABRIC_FAIL reports failure inside this switch.

concepts.label: after the node
concepts.gloss: At an observation point immediately downstream of the optical node.
concepts.example: Low channel power is measured after the ROADM whose attenuation drifted.

concepts.label: at the node
concepts.gloss: Within or at the boundary of the referenced network node.
concepts.example: Channels from one degree are blocked at the ROADM node.

concepts.label: Standard
concepts.gloss: A measurement or function supplied by default without an optional monitoring licence.
concepts.example: Received power and errored-seconds counters are available on a standard line card.

concepts.label: Power monitoring licence
concepts.gloss: An optional licence entitlement that exposes optical power measurements.
concepts.example: Enabling the power-monitoring licence provides composite EDFA input and output power.

concepts.label: Advanced monitoring licence
concepts.gloss: An optional licence entitlement that exposes advanced coherent-signal quality measurements.
concepts.example: The licence enables OSNR, pre-FEC BER, DGD, and SOP-rate telemetry.

concepts.label: 15-minute bins (standard)
concepts.gloss: Standard storage and reporting of performance counters in fixed 15-minute intervals.
concepts.example: Client ES and UAS are reported for the interval from 10:00 to 10:15.

concepts.label: OCM licence
concepts.gloss: An optional optical-channel-monitor licence that provides per-wavelength power and OSNR data.
concepts.example: With the OCM licence, the ROADM reports power for each WDM channel.

concepts.label: Hard
concepts.gloss: A fault nature representing an abrupt, persistent failure that typically causes immediate signal or service loss.
concepts.example: A fibre cut producing instant OCH_LOS is classified as hard.

concepts.label: Soft
concepts.gloss: A fault nature representing degradation that impairs quality while the signal may remain present and usable.
concepts.example: A 2 dB OSNR penalty causing OTU_SD is classified as soft.

concepts.label: Incipient
concepts.gloss: A fault nature representing an observable ageing trend or warning that precedes functional failure.
concepts.example: Rising laser-bias current before transmitter failure is classified as incipient.

concepts.label: Critical
concepts.gloss: The highest alarm severity for a condition requiring immediate attention because service or major network function is seriously affected.
concepts.example: A fabric failure interrupting all ODUs is assigned Critical severity.

concepts.label: Minor
concepts.gloss: A low alarm severity for a limited or nonurgent fault that does not yet cause major service impact.
concepts.example: An early ageing warning with service still healthy is assigned Minor severity.

concepts.label: Not alarmed
concepts.gloss: A severity state in which a condition is monitored or described but does not generate an alarm.
concepts.example: A normal operating observation is marked Not alarmed.

concepts.label: Major
concepts.gloss: A high alarm severity for a significant fault or service impact that is serious but below critical priority.
concepts.example: Loss of one client service due to port failure is assigned Major severity.

concepts.label: On loss of OTU frame, G.798 consequent actions apply: ODU-AIS is sent downstream on every ODU in the OTU, and OTU-BDI is returned to the far-end transmitter.
concepts.gloss: The G.798 OTU defect response that inserts ODU-AIS into every contained ODU downstream and returns OTU-BDI toward the transmitting endpoint after OTU frame loss.
concepts.example: When an OTU receiver loses frame, it sends AIS on all client ODUs and BDI back to the far-end transmitter.

concepts.label: Every hut terminates the optical supervisory channel (OSC) and launches its own OSC onto the next span.
concepts.gloss: The span-by-span supervisory-channel behavior in which each hut terminates the received OSC and originates a new OSC on the following span.
concepts.example: An amplifier hut consumes the west-span OSC and launches a separate OSC eastward.

concepts.label: Client services may be protected with SNCP: a working and a protection ODU path, with the selector at the receiving client port.
concepts.gloss: Subnetwork connection protection using working and protection ODU paths with receive-side selection at the destination client port.
concepts.example: If the working ODU develops AIS, the receiving port selects the defect-free protection ODU.

concepts.label: Switching is per channel at each egress degree. A line-wide impairment on an ingress degree therefore continues as a per-channel impairment on each channel routed onward.
concepts.gloss: ROADM forwarding behavior in which wavelengths are switched independently at each egress, so an ingress-wide impairment persists separately on every onward-routed channel.
concepts.example: All west-ingress channels share an OSNR penalty, then carry that penalty individually onto their different egress degrees.
